Seattle, Washington · eat

Restaurants in Seattle for cyclists

Where to eat in Seattle the night before and the afternoon after. Real food, open when you need it.

For: Seattle to Portland Bicycle Classic.

Restaurants in Seattle for cyclists, listed

  1. Un Bien (Seaview)

    The night-before sandwich on the Ballard side: a pink shack just off Shilshole Bay, on the road to Golden Gardens, where the Burke-Gilman starts.

    • Caribbean
    • 6226 Seaview Ave NW, Seattle, WA 98107
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Un Bien (Seaview)

    Roast pork sandwiches and plates. 11 to 9 Wednesday to Saturday, 11 to 8 Sunday, closed Monday and Tuesday, per its site. Pick-up orders by phone, (206) 420-7545. The Ballard sibling at 7302.5 15th Ave NW keeps the same hours. Seating and bike parking weren’t on the page.

  2. Marination Ma Kai

    After the ride, West Seattle: at Seacrest Park, the start of the West Seattle loop and the foot of the water taxi.

    • Hawaiian-Korean
    • 1660 Harbor Avenue SW, Seattle, WA 98126
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Marination Ma Kai

    Tacos, rice bowls and shave ice on a waterfront patio, indoor and outdoor, per its site. 11 to 8 Monday to Thursday, 11 to 9 Friday, from 9 on Saturday (to 9) and Sunday (to 8). Bike parking wasn’t on the page.

  3. Roanoke Inn

    On the way, Mercer Island: the tavern Cascade’s Mercer Island loop tells riders to stop at, a few blocks off the I-90 trail at the island’s north end.

    • Pub
    • 1825 72nd Ave SE, Mercer Island, WA 98040
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Roanoke Inn

    Porch, patio and a back yard. Open seven days except Thanksgiving and Christmas, per its site: 3 to 10 Monday, 11 to 10 Tuesday, 11 to midnight Wednesday to Saturday, 11 to 10 Sunday (Oct 2026). (206) 232-0800.

  4. Shultzy’s Bar & Grill

    The night before the STP, on the Ave in the U District: house-made sausage since 1988, a plate of carbs and protein.

    • Sausages and grill
    • 4114 University Way NE, Seattle, WA 98105
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Shultzy’s Bar & Grill

    Hours not confirmed since Sept 2026; check before you go.

  5. Cedars Restaurant

    The U District, a few blocks from the STP hotels: curries and kabobs, in the neighborhood since 1974.

    • Indian and Mediterranean
    • 4759 Brooklyn Ave NE, Seattle, WA 98105
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Cedars Restaurant

    Hours not confirmed since Sept 2026; check before you go.

  6. Big Time Brewery & Alehouse

    The U District’s brewpub, which calls itself “Seattle’s original brew pub,” since 1988.

    • Brewpub
    • 4133 University Way NE, Seattle, WA 98105
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Big Time Brewery & Alehouse

    Family-friendly, per its site. The beer the night before the STP, on the Ave. Hours not confirmed since Sept 2026; check before you go.

  7. Portage Bay Cafe

    After the ride, the U District: breakfast next door to the University Inn, local and organic in its own words.

    • Breakfast and brunch
    • 4130 Roosevelt Way NE, Seattle, WA 98105
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Portage Bay Cafe

    Opens 7:30 a.m. weekdays, 8 a.m. weekends, per its site (confirmed Sept 2026), so it is the morning after the STP, not the 5 a.m. start.

  8. Dick’s Drive-In (Broadway)

    Late, Capitol Hill: 10:30 a.m. to 2 a.m. every day, per its site, across from the Capitol Hill light rail station.

    • Burgers
    • 115 Broadway East, Seattle, WA 98102
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Dick’s Drive-In (Broadway)

    A walk-up window since 1955; stand in line, eat outside or take it away. Cheap. Not the night-before plate, but open when the day ran long and nothing else is.
